content_voiceover: This hexagon diagram summarizes the toxicity spectrum across all approved CML TKIs, which is high yield for boards. In the center are the common adverse effects shared by the whole class: myelosuppression, transaminase elevation, and electrolyte disturbances. Moving outward, imatinib is associated with edema and fluid retention, hypophosphatemia, GI upset, and rarely renal effects. Dasatinib's signature toxicities are pleural and pericardial effusion, pulmonary arterial hypertension, and bleeding risk. Bosutinib tends to cause diarrhea, nausea, and transaminitis. Nilotinib and ponatinib share the highest cardiovascular risk, boxed in red here: vascular adverse events, QT prolongation, hyperglycemia, and elevated lipase, plus pancreatic enzyme elevation and hyperbilirubinemia with nilotinib, and hypertension and pancreatitis with ponatinib. Asciminib, the newest agent, mainly causes thrombocytopenia and hypertension. For boards, remember dasatinib equals pleural effusion, nilotinib and ponatinib equal vascular risk, and imatinib equals edema.
keypoints: Common class AEs: myelosuppression, transaminitis, electrolyte changes
Dasatinib: pleural effusion, pulmonary hypertension, bleeding
Nilotinib and ponatinib carry the highest cardiovascular risk
Imatinib: edema and GI effects; bosutinib: diarrhea
keypoint_voiceover: Key takeaway: know each TKI's signature toxicity. Dasatinib causes pleural and pericardial effusions plus pulmonary hypertension. Nilotinib and ponatinib carry the greatest cardiovascular risk, including vascular events and QT prolongation. Imatinib is linked to edema and GI symptoms, while bosutinib causes diarrhea and transaminitis. All share myelosuppression and transaminase elevation as common effects.
